clue.text: Check collar

definitions.meaning: to check something is to stop or halt its progress
to collar someone is police slang for seizing a suspect

explanation.definitionFit: Both are synonyms: halting a decline and a police officer nabbing a suspect share this one verb.

clue.text: Novice with puppet is a great hit

parts.note: a rabbit is sporting slang for a poor or inexperienced player
Punch is the hook-nosed puppet of the British seaside Punch and Judy show

explanation.surface: A beginner with a glove puppet turns out to be a huge success.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hit' reads as a success but is a literal blow. Punch is the puppet in Punch and Judy, a traditional British seaside show.
explanation.definitionFit: It is an example of a heavy blow, a chop to the back of the neck.

clue.text: Limitless claret, say, for ancient king

indicators.note: without its limits, so the phrase loses its first and last letters

parts.note: claret is an example of red wine

explanation.surface: An old monarch is supplied with claret without end.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Limitless' strips the first and last letters, R and E, from RED WINE, the drink that claret exemplifies.
explanation.definitionFit: He is an example: a seventh-century ruler of Northumbria bore this name.

clue.text: Poor tenor — he'd a lamentable song

indicators.note: something poor is in a bad state, so the letters are put out of order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written, without the apostrophe

explanation.surface: A dreadful singer performed a truly awful number.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Poor' is the anagram signal for TENOR HED. 'Lamentable' pretends to mean dreadful but is literal: a song of lament.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a variant spelling of the word for a dirge, a song of mourning.

clue.text: Slightly crazy and spiteful after school

indicators.note: the word for spiteful is placed following the letter for school

parts.note: catty means spiteful or bitchy

explanation.surface: Someone turns a bit mad and malicious once lessons finish.
explanation.definitionFit: It is an informal synonym for scatterbrained or mildly mad.

clue.text: Holy man taking a learned theologian into quiet university

indicators.note: the article and the theologian go inside the word for quiet

parts.note: sh is an interjection asking for quiet
DD is Doctor of Divinity, a senior theology degree

explanation.surface: A guru escorts a scholarly divine to a peaceful college.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taking' only joins the definition to the wordplay; 'into' is the insertion signal. A Doctor of Divinity is the 'learned theologian'.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a variant spelling of the Hindu word for an ascetic sage.

clue.text: Plant adorns oar at sea

indicators.note: at sea means confused or lost, so the letters are thrown into disorder

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Greenery decorates a paddle on a boat out on the ocean.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at sea' is the anagram signal for ADORNS OAR, not a location.
explanation.definitionFit: It is an example: a common name for the tall yellow-flowered mullein.

clue.text: Fish without a vessel

indicators.note: the fish lacks the letter that the article supplies

parts.note: a tuna is a large sea fish

explanation.surface: Someone goes angling with no boat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' removes A from TUNA. The vessel is a large cask, not a boat.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a large cask for beer or wine, one kind of container.

clue.text: Fail to see short girl beneath bear

indicators.note: the word for girl is cut short, losing its last letter

parts.note: a miss is a girl or young woman
under is a synonym of beneath
to stand something is to bear or tolerate it

explanation.surface: A small child goes unnoticed underneath a large animal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'short' drops the last S from MISS. 'bear' is the verb meaning tolerate, not the animal, and 'see' means grasp.
explanation.definitionFit: To see is to grasp a point, so failing to do so is getting it wrong.

clue.text: Phone left out by prison for avid collector

indicators.note: the letter for left is taken out of the word for phone

parts.note: blower is British slang for the telephone
bird is British slang for a prison sentence, as in doing bird

explanation.surface: A mobile is abandoned outside a jail for a keen hoarder to find.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' removes L from BLOWER, British slang for the telephone; BIRD is British slang for time in jail.
explanation.definitionFit: The male famously gathers bright objects to decorate its courtship structure, a witty description.

clue.text: Group operating illegally call round

definitions.meaning: a criminal gang, as with drugs or spies

explanation.definitionFit: Three senses of one word: a criminal gang, to telephone, and a circle.

clue.text: Small and dainty starters of mince, gnocchi and onions

indicators.note: the opening letters of each dish are taken, here the first two of each

explanation.surface: Petite first courses of ground meat, potato dumplings and onions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'starters of' takes the first two letters of each of the three foods, not just one.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a French-derived adjective meaning delicately pretty and petite.

clue.text: Bats like sliding doors?

definitions.meaning: bats is slang for mad or deranged
sliding doors run on tracks, so they have no hinges

explanation.definitionFit: A synonym of deranged, and a whimsical literal description of a door lacking hinges.

clue.text: Topping official making you late for work

definitions.text: Topping official making you late for work

parts.words: Topping official making you late for work
parts.note: topping is slang for killing, especially by hanging, and late means dead: an official whose job is to kill

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a splendid bureaucrat delaying your commute; 'topping' is slang for hanging and 'late' means dead.
explanation.definitionFit: A hangman is an officer of the state whose job is putting the condemned to death.

clue.text: Fine cook lends dip

indicators.note: to cook is to prepare or concoct, so the letters are worked into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A good chef loans out some hummus.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cook' is an imperative anagram signal for LENDS DIP, not a noun.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a synonym for excellent or magnificent.

clue.text: Person ate horrible artificial tongue

indicators.note: horrible suggests something in a nasty state, so the letters are disordered

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Somebody ate a nasty fake ox tongue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'horrible' is the anagram signal for PERSON ATE. The tongue is a language, not meat.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a constructed language, invented by Zamenhof in 1887.

clue.text: Taking top off fish basket reveals this part of angler's kit

indicators.note: the top of the word is its first letter, which is removed

parts.note: a creel is a wicker basket for carrying caught fish

explanation.surface: Lifting the lid of a wicker basket shows a piece of fishing tackle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Taking top off' removes C, the first letter of CREEL.
explanation.definitionFit: It is an example of fishing tackle: the spool holding the line.

clue.text: Obese lot struggling being out of practice

indicators.note: struggling suggests thrashing about, so the letters are jumbled

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A very overweight group labour because they have not trained lately.
explanation.walkthrough: 'struggling' is the anagram signal for OBESE LOT. 'out of practice' means no longer practised, not rusty.
explanation.definitionFit: Something no longer practised or used has fallen into disuse.

clue.text: Cut and scratch from a vegetable

indicators.note: the word for scratch is taken away from the vegetable

parts.note: a parsnip is a pale root vegetable
in golf, scratch means a handicap of zero, playing to par

explanation.surface: Someone gets a nick and a graze while peeling a root.
explanation.walkthrough: 'from' removes PAR, a golfer's scratch score, from PARSNIP.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a synonym as noun or verb: a small quick slice with scissors.

clue.text: Radioactive stuff symbolically found in heart of turbot

parts.words: symbolically found in heart of turbot
parts.note: the chemical symbol of this element is the two middle letters of the fish's name

explanation.surface: A hazardous substance is detected in the organs of a flatfish.
explanation.walkthrough: The middle letters of 'turbot' are RB, the chemical symbol; 'symbolically' says the element is present only as its symbol.
explanation.definitionFit: It is an alkali metal whose commonest natural isotope mix is slightly unstable.

clue.text: Harry set about extremely dated puzzle

indicators.note: the word for harry is placed around the other letters

parts.note: to harry is to harass or annoy, to rile

indicators.note: the extremes of a word are its first and last letters

explanation.surface: Harry started tackling a very old-fashioned brain-teaser.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Harry' wants to be a man's name; it is the verb meaning to harass. 'set about' is the container signal and 'extremely' picks the first and last letters of 'dated'.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a synonym: a conundrum or enigma.

clue.text: Chief constable, say, is a social reformer

parts.note: John Constable was an English landscape painter, so an example of an artist

explanation.surface: A senior police officer is, for instance, a campaigner for change.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Chief constable' is split: 'constable' is John Constable, the English landscape painter, hidden by the lower-case c.
explanation.definitionFit: He was a member of the 1830s-40s British working-class movement demanding electoral rights.

clue.text: Conservative took cover behind yellow plant

indicators.note: the first two pieces of the clue follow the word for yellow

parts.note: or is the heraldic term for gold or yellow
hid means concealed oneself

explanation.surface: A Tory ducked out of sight at the back of a golden shrub.
explanation.walkthrough: 'yellow' is the heraldic word for gold, a crossword staple; 'behind' orders the pieces, so the Tory and his hiding come second.
explanation.definitionFit: It is an example: an exotic flowering species.

clue.text: Councillor and one politician wave

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
an MP is a Member of Parliament

explanation.surface: A local representative and a member of parliament greet the crowd.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wave' is a verb of hairdressing here, not a hand gesture.
explanation.definitionFit: To put tight curls or ripples into hair is to do this.

clue.text: Immediately like the other set of clues

definitions.meaning: paid on the spot, as in cash on the nail

definitions.text: like the other set of clues
definitions.meaning: this clue is an across, so the other set are those running vertically

explanation.definitionFit: Money paid on the spot and the vertical direction of crossword entries share this word.

clue.text: Topless yob's unconscious

indicators.note: in a down clue the top is the first letter, which is removed

parts.note: a yob is British slang for a lout or hooligan

explanation.surface: A shirtless hooligan lies knocked senseless.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Topless' removes L, the first letter of LOUT; a yob is British slang for a hooligan.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a synonym, as in knocked cold.

clue.text: Academic tours a new food shop for some salad leaves

indicators.note: to tour is to go round, so the academic goes around the other pieces

parts.note: a don is a university teacher, especially at Oxford or Cambridge
a deli is a delicatessen

explanation.surface: A professor visits a newly opened delicatessen to buy greens.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tours' looks like a visit to the shop but is the container signal: the academic goes round everything else.
explanation.definitionFit: Its young leaves are eaten raw as greens, so the plant is one source.

clue.text: Tried hard to put last bit of dinner in oven

indicators.note: the single letter is placed inside the word for oven

parts.note: a stove is a cooker

indicators.note: the last bit of a word is its final letter

explanation.surface: A cook made every effort to get the final course baked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' places R, picked by 'last bit of' from 'dinner', inside STOVE.
explanation.definitionFit: It is the past tense of the verb meaning to struggle or make great efforts.

clue.text: Skilful poise adopted in river — right on time

indicators.note: something adopted is taken in, so the letter sits inside the river

parts.note: the Exe is a river in Devon, south-west England
the poise is a unit of viscosity, abbreviated P

explanation.surface: A graceful stance is struck in the stream, punctually.
explanation.walkthrough: 'adopted in' puts P inside EXE, a river in Devon. 'Poise' is the physics unit of viscosity, not balance.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a synonym as an adjective: highly practised and adept.
